summary.headline: CreditAccess Grameen posted record Q2 FY27 PAT of INR 502 Crore, raised FY27 ROA guidance to 5.2%-5.8% and ROE to 21%-24%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 PAT hit a record INR 502 Crore and H1 PAT reached INR 995 Crore versus INR 778 Crore in H1 FY26, with H1 ROA at 5.9% and ROE at 23.8%. AUM grew 19.5% YoY to INR 30,946 Crore, while the Group Loan book declined 2% since the start of FY27 due to write-offs and graduation. Asset quality improved sequentially (GNPA 1.79%, NNPA 0.59%), but management flagged a rise in PAR accretion in August-September from floods and festivities and early drought stress in about 6 Maharashtra districts. Management raised FY27 profitability guidance and cut its NIM guidance sharply upward, while passing a 50 bps lending rate cut from October.

segments.name: Group Loans
segments.commentary: Book at INR 23,746 Crore as of September 2026, down 2% from start of FY27 due to write-offs and graduation; INR 614 Crore written off in H1 mostly from Group Loans. Management expects return to guided growth in H2.

segments.name: Retail Finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR 7,200 Crore, 23.3% of total AUM (20.6% in Q1 FY27). Secured book (secured business loans, affordable housing, 2-wheeler) grew 60.9% YoY to INR 695 Crore; 2-wheeler book crossed INR 60 Crore from INR 20 Crore in Q1.

segments.name: Mortgage
segments.commentary: Operates from 428 branches per Q&A, up from 120 earlier; management says NPAs rising but within tolerance, budgeting about 2% credit cost in mortgage.

segments.name: Individual Business Loans
segments.commentary: Graduation product (Unnati average tenure over 7 years, average credit score above 730); PAR 30 has not crossed 3% even at the peak of the credit cycle.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ROA guidance raised to 5.2%-5.8% from 4%-4.8%; ROE raised to 21%-24% from 16%-20%.
FY27 NIM guidance of 14.4%-14.7%, up from 12.8%-13.2% earlier, after factoring a 50 bps lending rate cut from October.
AUM growth guidance of 20%-25% retained; Microfinance seen range-bound at 10%-12% growth while retail grows faster.

Credit cost guidance of 3%-4% maintained; H1 run-rate about 3%, Q3 expected to inch up, with ECL provisioning rising 5-6 bps per quarter in Q3 and Q4. Management said credit cost likely 3.5%-4% for FY27.
Cost-to-income guided to 29%-30%. A further 50 bps lending rate cut is planned for Q3 FY27 (about INR 50 bps in next quarter); subsequent cuts depend on credit cost holding near 3%.
Borrowing cost expected to stay in 9.2%-9.3% range till March 2027; yield cut of 50 bps to flow through over 4-6 quarters.
Insurance commission regulation could reduce ROA by 25-30 bps; management says pricing could offset it.
capex_capacity: Expanded to 2,326 branches across 460 districts after opening 60 branches in Q2 FY27.
Mortgage presence across 300 GL branches and 128 Retail Finance branches; 2-wheeler loans via 950-plus Group Loan branches.
Dedicated collection team of 500-plus employees; additional collection resources deployed in Maharashtra.
Mortgage expansion target of a few hundred branches every year.
Target of more than 1 lakh new customers per month; currently about 80,000 per month.
demand_pricing: Q2 new borrowers 2.3 lakh (35% new-to-credit); H1 additions 4.9 lakh; total borrowers about 45 lakh, with Retail Finance 6.8 lakh (15%).
Borrower retention improved to 88% in H1 FY27 from 85% in FY26; 3 lakh customers written off in past 12 months.
Industry: banks have significantly pulled back from microfinance, while MFIs and NBFCs gained share; management sees no broad pullback by large players.
Gold loan exposure stable at about 10-12% of overall customer base.
Lending rate cut of 50 bps across products except mortgage and 2-wheeler; the company is among the lowest-priced lenders in microfinance.
Drought-related requests for time or restructuring seen in about 6 central Maharashtra districts; no on-ground impact seen elsewhere in October.

qa_highlights.question: Why cut lending rates by 50 bps now when marginal borrowing cost rose 25-30 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIMs are at highest levels and the cut follows the pricing policy; borrowing cost is expected at 9.2%-9.3% through March as ECB refinancing replaces higher-cost debt. Risk-adjusted NIM is about 11%, with a target of 10%.

qa_highlights.question: How will credit cost trend in Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q3 to inch up; even a 5% H2 run-rate would keep FY27 within 4%. Management guided FY27 credit cost to 3.5%-4%.

qa_highlights.question: Are flood and PAR accretion spikes in UP, Bihar, MP and Tamil Nadu continuing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said September spikes were due to floods and festivities; October was normal everywhere except Maharashtra. Credit cost spike beyond 5% is the pricing threshold.

qa_highlights.question: How much exposure is in drought-affected districts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 6 central Maharashtra districts are affected, but portfolio share was not available and would be provided offline.

qa_highlights.question: Is a guarantee scheme in place for microfinance?
qa_highlights.answer: No microfinance guarantee yet; CGFMU application pending budget approval, expected to open in a week or two. Premium about 1.3%-1.5% annually covering about 75% of losses. Smaller CGTMSE and BII guarantees exist for individual lending.

qa_highlights.question: Why is borrower growth in single digits and what is the customer acquisition plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said write-offs and attrition held the count down; customer acquisition expected to show improvement in Q3 and Q4. Management targets over 1 lakh customers per month, versus about 80,000 now.

risks_watch: Drought stress in central Maharashtra and whether it spreads beyond the 6 districts in November-December.
Credit cost trajectory in Q3-Q4 FY27 and its effect on FY28 pricing and ROA; pricing cushion holds up to about 4.5%-5% credit cost.
Insurance commission regulation could reduce ROA by 25-30 bps.
Group Loan book recovery and customer acquisition pace; borrower count growth remains weak.
Mortgage asset quality rising from low base; management budgeting 2% credit cost.
Borrowing cost could rise if repo-linked exposure reprices faster than MCLR-linked debt; management says 9.2%-9.3% range through March.
Promoter-level strategic investor discussions at holding level, timing undefined.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, guidance and asset quality, but cautious on drought exposure and Q3 credit cost. Management gave few specifics on customer acquisition timing and the Maharashtra district portfolio share, deferring them to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: We reported our highest quarterly profit of INR 502 Crore in this quarter, having grown fivefold over the past 5 years.
We're maintaining our credit cost guidance of 3% to 4%, and it should comfortably cover for any volatility on account of evolving drought-related conditions in some operating geographies.
Our risk -adjusted NIMs are currently at highest levels.
